Santería.question: What do you know about Santería (Spanish pronunciation: [san.te.ˈɾi.a]), also called Regla de Ocha, Reg?
Santería.answer: an African diaspora religion that developed in Cuba during the late 19th century. There is no central authority in contr
Santería.fact: Santería (Spanish pronunciation: [san.te.ˈɾi.a]), also called Regla de Ocha, Regla Lucumí, or Lucumí, is an African diaspora religion that developed in Cuba during the late 19th century. There is no central authority in control of Santería and much diversity exists among practitioners, who are called creyentes ('believers').

Santería.fact: In urban areas of West Cuba, these traditions merged with Spiritist ideas to form the earliest ilés during the late 19th century.

Santería.fact: Santería's roots are in the traditional religions brought to Cuba by enslaved West Africans, the majority of them Yoruba, between the 16th and 19th centuries. Roman Catholic saints were conflated with West African deities, while enslaved Africans adopted Roman Catholic rituals and sacramentals.
